title: Three ways bacteria exchange genes
caption: In transformation a bacterium takes up free DNA from its surroundings. In transduction a bacteriophage carries DNA from one bacterium to another. In conjugation two bacteria join through a pilus and usually pass a plasmid through it. All three are horizontal transfer, unlike vertical transfer from parent to offspring.
alt: Three panels. Transformation: free DNA fragments above a bacterium and an arrow into it. Transduction: a bacteriophage between two bacteria with an arrow to the lower one. Conjugation: two bacteria joined by a pilus, a plasmid shown between them.
description: Transformation: uptake of free DNA from the environment.
Transduction: transfer of DNA by a bacteriophage.
Conjugation: direct transfer, usually of a plasmid, through a pilus.
These spread antibiotic resistance and virulence genes between bacteria.
